name: PoleLine
subtitle: Draw the lap. Take pole.
shortDescription: Draw your racing line and watch the car run it. Twenty circuits, all offline.
description:
A great lap starts with a line.

Pick your tyres, draw your racing line around the circuit with one finger, and watch a modern single-seater drive exactly that line in real time: live sectors, gear, revs, active aero, battery and tyre temperature. Then read the result. Which sector cost you? Did the softs overheat? Did the battery clip early? Draw again.

Twenty circuits of your own
From the tight streets of Harbour Loop to the long, cold sweeps of Aurora Point: street circuits at night, fast parks, hairpins, esses and a short club circuit. Each one has its own locked conditions, so every lap is comparable. A guided first lap on the Rookie Ring teaches the game in a minute, and you can pause it to change how you draw.

Your line is the lap
Lay it your way. Easy: for each segment of the lap, tap Gas or Brake, and Left or Right to move your line across the road, then see exactly where the lap lost time. Medium: tap the track and bend the curves. Hard: draw freely and each stroke is tidied into a racing line. Expert: every inch is yours, and the white line stops you. The car cannot follow a wobble, so a smooth, wide entry and a clipped apex beat a short cut. Pole pace, a grid slot from P1 to P20 and a race engineer's note tell you where the time is.

Your times, your device
Your ten quickest laps on every circuit stay on your phone with their lines. Watch any of them again against your best, and reuse the drawing setup it was set with. No account, no ads, no in-app purchases, no analytics and no internet connection. The only permission it uses is vibration.

Pick your car's colours from nine teams, or keep the PoleLine purple.

PoleLine is a Toyboxes game by Randroid LLC.
releaseNotes: First release: twenty circuits, four ways to lay your racing line from a segment by segment pad to pure freehand, tyre strategy, where each lap lost time, your ten quickest laps per circuit with replays, a guided first lap, and nothing that needs a connection.
playReleaseNotes: New: four ways to lay your racing line. Easy, the new default, goes segment by segment: tap Gas or Brake, and Left or Right to move your line across the road, then see where the lap lost time. Medium lays curves you tap and bend, Hard tidies each stroke, Expert is pure freehand. Turn numbers and sectors now mark every circuit, the lap closes cleanly on the start point, and you can open any saved lap to change part of it.
reviewNotes: No login or network connection is needed. The first launch opens a guided lap on the Rookie Ring; its welcome card offers Easy, Medium, Hard or Expert (Easy is picked, and Skip is available). On Easy the lap is laid up to the last corner: tap Gas or Brake for each segment (Left or Right moves the line across the road), then pick a tyre and tap Race. After that, pick a circuit and tap Draw a lap. Easy lays the whole lap the same way. On Medium, choose a tyre, touch the chequered line, tap the track ahead to lay curves and tap further on or Set curve; on Hard and Expert, drag along the road, lift, and carry on from the purple tip. The car runs the line when the lap closes. Your times are stored on the device. This is a paid download without ads or in-app purchases.
